_note: The adversarial trace is the milestone's real acceptance test: the three M0 fixture sets exercise capture and not tamper evidence at all. Four attacks are planted and four findings are expected of them. Every other code in `finding_codes` is attributed to a named cause below; none is left unexplained.
_generated_from_a_real_run: This file was written from `goalcup-verify crates/goalcup-verifier/tests/fixtures/adversarial` and then read by eye, not predicted. If a change makes it wrong, read the verdict before editing the file: regenerate the fixture (scripts/regen-adversarial-fixture.md), run the binary, and decide whether the new reading is the truth about the planted bytes.
_finding_codes_are_review_queue_codes: `finding_codes` names codes that appear in `Verdict::review_queue`, which holds Flag and Fail findings only, and which is the union of every check's findings AND the seal findings `verify_trace` raises outside any check. A Pass-level code (`anchors_checked`, `anchor_timeline`, `goal_recovered`, `one_tracked_session`, `join_key_agrees`, `normalisation_applied`, `no_version_drift`, `token_summary`) is a statement the verdict makes and never a queue entry, so none is listed here. The list is compared for SET EQUALITY, as in `end_to_end.rs`: a code listed that the run does not raise, and a code raised that is not listed, both fail.
_this_is_a_pure_chain_trace: As of 2026-09-04 the fixture declares one `chain.jsonl`, the two manifests the chain's own links cover (`baseline.json` at seq 0 and `seal.json` at the head) and nothing else: no `[[leg1]]` store, no `[leg2]` table, and no `main.jsonl`, `subagent.jsonl` or `hooks.jsonl` beside the descriptor. Leg-1 records are `Leg1Record` envelopes, leg-2 posts are `Leg2Post` envelopes, and the seal is the chain's last link, all written through `goalcup_protocol::export::TraceExport`. A store the descriptor named beside a chain would be an off-chain side channel — bytes the verifier reads that the chain never covered — and `TraceDescriptor::load` now refuses one. The four planted attacks are unchanged and all four still fire; what moved is which path the fixture measures, and it is now the path the daemon actually produces.
_the_baseline_is_the_chains_first_link: NOT a fifth planted attack. The 2026-09-04 fix wave made the R3 baseline a chained link, and this trace now carries an EMPTY one at seq 0: the workspace this run started in held nothing, which is exactly what makes `planted.txt` a planted file rather than one the directory came with. Before the fix `baseline.json` was written by the participant's own daemon and covered by nothing, so a pre-populated workspace could be entered into it wholesale and every planted file would read as `Attribution::Baseline`. Two consequences here, and both are deliberate. First, `baseline_missing` and `baseline_not_chained` are BOTH absent: the descriptor names the file, the chain's first link is a baseline, and `baseline.json` hashes to the digest that link claims. Second, every seq in this file is one higher than it was, because a link was inserted below the whole chain — the two acknowledgements, the unanchored windows and the heartbeat hole all moved together, and none of the four planted attacks changed. `seal.json` did not move a byte.
_cause_ack_chain_mismatch: PLANTED 1, x1, Fail. The first assistant record at or after chain seq 30 was rewritten before the chain was built over it, and the acknowledgement at seq 100 carries the hash the honest chain would have held there. Exactly one mismatch, at seq 100; the acknowledgement at seq 20 sits below the rewrite and still reconciles, which is what places the edit between the two. Both acknowledgements name a position in the entry's ONE chain — `main` is chained first above the R3 baseline, which is seq 0, so a main record's chain seq is its position in the harness's own file PLUS ONE. The generator looks the two acknowledged links up by chain sequence rather than indexing the store, so the constants keep meaning what they say.
_cause_store_rewritten: PLANTED 2, x1, Fail. `chain.jsonl` carries a `TailNotice { kind: truncated }` for `main`: offset 157703 -> 0, inode unchanged. No traced tool call names the path and no expected re-read is declared anywhere, so V9's two escape hatches are both closed. `offset_before` is the store's real length in bytes — the sum of the harness lines the generator chained — and `adversarial.rs` reads it back out of that envelope rather than measuring a file, because a pure chain trace has no store file to measure.
_cause_unexplained_seal_file: PLANTED 3, x1, Fail. `planted.txt` is in `seal.json` and nothing in the trace names it. Raised by `verify_trace` from `seal_attribution`, not by any check. `hello.py` in the same seal attributes to a traced `Bash` call, so this is the attributor distinguishing two files rather than failing both — asserted directly in `adversarial.rs`.
_cause_dirty_gap: PLANTED 4, x1, Fail. The heartbeat series stops at 07:44:00Z and resumes at 08:05:00Z, and 40 of `main`'s records carry HARNESS timestamps inside that window. Raised on the one gap whose `is_hole` is true. The claim is a harness-timestamp claim on purpose, and `seq` could not make it: the generator chains all 165 leg-1 records first and the daemon's eight heartbeats after them, so those 40 sit at chain seq 90-143, BELOW the beat that closes the hole (seq 220) and the one that reopens it (seq 221), with nothing between the two in sequence. Read by `seq` the hole is empty; read by the harness's own clock the 40 are inside it — which is the reading `gaps::records_in_window` takes for an entry-chain store.
_unplaceable_records_left_on_2026_09_04: This file used to carry `unplaceable_records` x7 in `finding_codes`. It is gone, and the reason is the fixture becoming a pure chain trace rather than any weakening of the check. `unplaceable_records` is what a LEGACY store says when it cannot place a record in time: its sequences are the verifier's own per-store counter, so a record with no timestamp cannot be put inside or outside a window at all. An entry-chain record always can be placed — by the harness's timestamp where it has one, and by the chain's own order where it does not — so the reason is unreachable for this trace by construction. `main`'s 46 untimestamped records are still in the chain, still counted, and still reported: they are inside the `unanchored_records` windows below. The finding kept its coverage in `gaps.rs`'s own unit tests, which is where a per-store store with no timestamps is measured.
_cause_unanchored_records: Consequence of PLANTED 1, x3, Fail. The acknowledgement at seq 100 is the one the rewrite broke, so it is a mismatch and never enters `verified`. The highest verified sequence is therefore 20, and everything above it is chain nobody witnessed: `main`'s 128 records (seq 21..148), `subagent`'s 17 (seq 149..165), and the planted hole itself, which closes at chain seq 221 — far above the anchor. Three windows, one code. Every one of these numbers is one higher than it was before 2026-09-04, and for one reason: the baseline now occupies seq 0 and pushed the whole chain up by a link. `main` gains its 128th unanchored record for the same reason — the anchor is still chain seq 20, and one more of `main`'s records now sits above it. It was x1 while the two stores carried their own per-store sequences, which happened to sit below the acknowledged number; in the entry's one chain they no longer do, and that is the honest reading rather than a new fault.

_v10_became_pass_on_2026_09_04: This file used to carry V10's flag for a store declaring no `partition_key` in `finding_codes`, with a `_cause_` note beside it, and V10 was `flag` on that one code alone. The code is deleted: it read `connectors/claude-code-cli/manifest.toml` rather than these planted bytes, so it was a manifest defect reported once per run. `ConnectorManifest::validate()` now refuses a store that declares neither a `partition_key` nor an `unpartitioned_reason`, and the manifest's `main` and `raw_bodies` carry the reason (spike 4 A9: the config dir is a per-run process-scoped pin). _two_leg1_stores: The chain carries `main` and `subagent`, as the M0 claude-code-cli descriptor declares them, because the harness wrote both. Declaring only `main` produced a spurious `leg2_tool_without_leg1_call` and V8 `flag`: the hook stream posts a tool response whose call lives in the subagent's own file. With that store present V8 is `pass` and the code is gone, which is why it now sits in `must_not_contain`. The A9 `a9-other-folder.jsonl` probe stays absent — it is the M0 set's foreign-session exhibit, which is why `foreign_session` and `second_root_thread` are not in this list.
_cause_receipt_missing: NOT a fifth planted attack — a consequence of what this fixture is. V13 (the trace is bound to a server-signed start and closes at the run's deadline) joined on 2026-09-04 and reports `receipt_missing` (x1, Fail) on any trace that declares a `chain` and no `receipt`. This descriptor declares no receipt because the M0 capture it derives from predates the start receipt entirely: there is no server that issued one, so the generator has none to write and inventing one would mean this fixture signing its own start. The honest reading is the one V13 states — nothing outside the participant's machine says this run was ever declared — and it stands beside the four planted attacks rather than among them, which is why `tamper_findings` is unchanged. Every other V13 code is absent and stays absent. `receipt_invalid`, `receipt_unverified`, `descriptor_mismatch`, `chain_head_mismatch`, `window_unmeasurable`, `window_unplaceable`, `outside_window`, `pre_start_records`, `pre_start_records_early` and `binding_checked` all sit BELOW the `receipt_missing` early return, so a trace carrying no receipt at all can reach none of them — `receipt_unverified` in particular is what a receipt that WAS carried and checked against nothing raises, and this fixture has no receipt to leave unchecked. `chain_broken` because the chain is built by `TraceExport` and recomputes end to end (the rewrite is BELOW the acknowledgement, not below a link); `seal_not_chained` because the seal is `write_seal`'s own last link and its digest is the digest of the bytes in `seal.json`; `legacy_trace` because this descriptor declares a `chain`. `baseline_missing` and `baseline_not_chained` are the exception to that reading: they are raised OUTSIDE the receipt's early return, exactly as `seal_not_chained` is, so both were reachable here and both are silent because the baseline really is this chain's first link — see the note above. The 2026-09-04 fix wave moved no entry of `finding_codes`; it did move bytes, because the baseline link shifted every seq by one. The M1b window ruling — a record below `started_at` is `pre_start_records` at Pass or `pre_start_records_early` at Flag, never `outside_window` — moved nothing here at all: both codes sit below the same early return, and regenerating this fixture after it produced a byte-for-byte identical directory. Both connector-DIRECTORY codes are absent for the same reason, and the note that used to sit here explaining a `connector_dir_unbound` Flag went with them in fix round 1: `connector_dir_unpinned` and `connector_dir_unbound` are read out of a receipt whose signature verified, and this fixture carries no receipt at all. A Flag saying the connector directory was not named would have been the same absence `receipt_missing` already reports, said a second time.
_cause_placeholder_server_key: NOT a fifth planted attack — a consequence of what every fixture in this crate signs with. Added 2026-09-05 by the fix wave. `SERVER_PUBLIC_KEYS` holds one entry, `PLACEHOLDER_SERVER_PUBLIC_KEY`, whose private seed `[5u8; 32]` is written in this repository so the fixtures can sign at all; this descriptor names that key and the acknowledgement at seq 20 verifies against it, so the key was USED and V13 says so (x1, Flag). Anybody holding the repository can mint a receipt or an ack that reads as `key_source: "pinned"`, which is the strongest provenance a verdict has, so a Flag is the only honest way to spend that word. Nothing about the four planted attacks changed: `overall` is still `fail`, the exit code is still 2, V13 is still `fail` on `receipt_missing`, and `tamper_findings` is untouched. `server_key_unpinned` — the other half of the same fix-wave finding — is absent, because this trace's key IS pinned; that it is pinned to a published seed is what this code says. Replacing the placeholder with the real organiser key is the release gate before any entry is judged, and it will delete this entry from this file.
_parser_census_is_a_statement_not_a_find: `parser_census`: the record kinds the parser recognised and deliberately ignored, counted (`ParsedLegs::census`). A statement, never a finding — not a fifth planted attack, and no entry of `finding_codes` moved for it. It is identical to the M0 claude-code-cli trace's census because this fixture chains that capture's `main` and `subagent` and nothing else; the A9 probe, the only `foreign = true` store in the M0 set, is absent from this fixture entirely (see `_two_leg1_stores`). This trace carries no `truncated_tail` either: the chain `TraceExport` writes ends in a newline, so there is no half-written line to report.
first_human_message: create hello.py that prints the current date, run it, then tell me the output
_nine_findings_became_pass_level_on_2026: Task 13, and NOT a fifth planted attack — no tamper finding moved. Nine informational findings fired at Flag on every honest trace, which put them in `review_queue` and made `Severity::Pass` unreachable for a run that broke no rule; they are now Pass-level, so every sentence still appears in `Verdict::checks` and none appears in the queue. Four left this file's `finding_codes`, and all four were inherited from the M0 Claude script rather than planted here: `cross_leg_identifiers` (V3), `resume` (V4), `model_changed` (V5) and `user_slot_excluded` (V6) — their `_cause_` notes above still describe what the verdict says, at the severity it now says it. Two check verdicts moved with them: V5 and V6 are now `pass`. V3 stays `flag` on `leg2_without_leg1_record` and V4 stays `fail` on the planted `dirty_gap`, so PLANTED 4 is untouched. `clean_gap` also became Pass-level in the same change. Its entry in `must_not_contain` is now vacuous — that list is compared against the review queue, which a Pass-level code can never reach — and it stays because the claim it records is still true and is asserted where it can be: `adversarial.rs` reads the classified gaps directly and requires this trace's one hole to be `GapKind::Dirty`.
_must_name_is_one_needle_per_planted_att: `planted.txt` is the seal file nothing explains; `seq 100` is the acknowledged sequence the rewrite moved out from under; `truncated below the saved offset` is the tail notice; and the two heartbeat timestamps bound the hole the store grew inside. Note what is NOT here: the truncated store's path. V9 cites `store`, `seq` and `hash` and never interpolates a filesystem path, so no finding names `95addb64.jsonl` — the descriptor's tracked session id reaches a reader through `one_tracked_session`, which is a Pass and therefore not in the queue.
_neither_v12_timing_flag_fires_here: V12's two timing codes are `late_first_anchor` (the first verified acknowledgement is more than a day after the run's declared start) and `long_unanchored_span` (the longest stretch with no verified acknowledgement is more than a day, counting the one from the last acknowledgement to the end of the run). Both are silent on this fixture and both are listed below so a run that started raising one is read in a diff. `late_first_anchor` cannot fire: this descriptor declares no receipt, so there is no declared start to measure a first anchor against — which is `receipt_missing`, already noted above, and not a second finding. `long_unanchored_span` does not fire because the numbers are small: both acknowledgements carry `acked_at` 2026-09-03T07:45:00Z, so every span between them is 0s, and the chain's own seal link is dated 2026-09-03T08:10:00Z, so the tail is 1500s. The generator was not touched to arrange that; it is what the M0 capture the fixture derives from actually took.
